newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas retraces losses, big players active.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas retraces losses, big players active.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures strengthened on Thursday, retracing Wednesday's losses as big players moved in to buy, brokers said.
"It is almost the mirror image of yesterday, but just as busy," said one.
A total of 530 lots traded, close to the contract's record volume of 575 lots. Open interest stood at 2,825 lots at the end of the afternoon session.
Brokers said that at least two major players on the over-the-counter (OTC) market had bought up futures in an effort to push up market levels.
Brokers noted that such action would usually be confined to the OTC market, but said that the anonymity of the futures market looked to have attracted the buyers.
"This is the sort of thing that we'd usually see on the OTC market, but I think they're being drawn to the IPE because it's anonymous," said one.
Others noted that the relative illiquidity of the IPE contract offered players the opportunity to shift prices on small volumes.
The front month May ended the day at 10.175 pence a therm (p/th), having held support at 10 p/th.
Smaller gains were seen across the summer, while all the winter months climbed 0.10 p/th, with February boasting the highest price of 16.40 p/th.
April 1998 was the only loser, shedding 0.075 p/th to 12.375 p/th.
